concepts.title: Meaning of Percentage
concepts.definition: Per cent means per hundred. 1% = 1/100 = 0.01. Percentage is the numerator of a fraction with denominator 100.
concepts.key_idea: Per cent = per hundred. percentage = (part/total) x 100.
question_patterns: percentage when total is not hundred
what per cent of figure is shaded
out of 25 children 15 are girls what percentage

solution_steps.explain: Identify the part and the total

concepts.title: Converting Fractions to Percentage
concepts.definition: To convert a fraction to percentage, multiply by 100 and add %. percentage = fraction x 100%.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply fraction by 100 to get percentage.
question_patterns: convert fractional numbers to per cents

concepts.title: Converting Decimals to Percentage
concepts.definition: To convert a decimal to percentage, multiply by 100 and add %. 0.75 = 75%.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply decimal by 100 to get percentage.
question_patterns: convert given decimals to per cents

concepts.title: Converting Percentages to Fractions or Decimals
concepts.definition: To convert percentage to fraction: divide by 100 and simplify. To convert to decimal: divide by 100. Parts always add to 100%.
concepts.formula: percentage -> fraction: divide by 100; percentage -> decimal: divide by 100
concepts.key_idea: Divide percentage by 100 to get fraction or decimal.
question_patterns: convert per cents to decimal fractions
if 65 per cent have bicycle what per cent do not

solution_steps.explain: Take the number without the % sign
For fraction: write as numerator/100 and simplify. For decimal: shift decimal 2 places left.
State the resulting fraction or decimal in simplest form

concepts.title: Interpreting Percentages
concepts.definition: Interpreting a percentage means understanding what it represents. 5% of income saved means 5 out of every 100 rupees is saved.
concepts.formula: x% means x out of every 100
question_patterns: 5 per cent of income saved meaning

solution_steps.explain: x% means x out of every 100
Confirm the percentage correctly represents the given context

concepts.title: Converting Percentages to How Many
concepts.definition: To find how many when a percentage is given: count = (percentage / 100) x total. To find the whole when a percentage of it is known: whole = (part / percentage) x 100.
concepts.key_idea: Find count: (pct/100) x total. Find whole: part/pct x 100.
question_patterns: 25 per cent of 40 children like football how many
9 is 25 per cent of what number
75 per cent of what number is 15
saved 200 when discount 25 per cent find original price
meeta saves 4000 which is 10 per cent of salary find salary
find the whole quantity if 5 per cent is 600

concepts.title: Ratios to Percents
concepts.definition: To convert a ratio to percentage, find the fraction each part represents, then multiply by 100. For ratio a:b, percentage of a = (a/(a+b)) x 100.
concepts.formula: for ratio a:b:c, percentage of a = (a/(a+b+c)) x 100
concepts.key_idea: Each part's fraction = part/total. Percentage = fraction x 100.
question_patterns: two parts rice one part dal find percentage
divide 250 amongst ravi raju roy in ratio 2:3:5
divide 15 sweets 20 per cent and 80 per cent
angles of triangle in ratio 2:3:4 find each
chalk contains calcium carbon oxygen in ratio 10:3:12

solution_steps.explain: total = sum of all ratio parts

concepts.title: Increase or Decrease as Per Cent
concepts.definition: Percentage change = (amount of change / original amount) x 100. For increase: change = new - original. For decrease: change = original - new.
question_patterns: won 6 games this year 4 last year per cent increase
illiterate persons decreased from 150 to 100 lakhs
petrol from 1 to 52 per litre percentage increase

solution_steps.explain: If new > original, increase. If new < original, decrease.

concepts.title: Profit and Loss
concepts.definition: Cost Price (CP) is the buying price. Selling Price (SP) is the selling price. If SP > CP, profit = SP - CP. If CP > SP, loss = CP - SP. If CP = SP, no profit no loss.
concepts.formula: profit = SP - CP (when SP > CP); loss = CP - SP (when CP > SP)
concepts.key_idea: Profit = SP - CP. Loss = CP - SP.
question_patterns: tell what is profit or loss

solution_steps.explain: CP = cost price, SP = selling price
If SP > CP: profit = SP - CP. If CP > SP: loss = CP - SP.

concepts.title: Profit or Loss as Percentage
concepts.definition: Profit % = (profit / CP) x 100. Loss % = (loss / CP) x 100. Always calculated on CP.
concepts.key_idea: Profit/Loss percentage is always on CP.
question_patterns: bought for 375 sold for 400 find gain percentage
cost 50 sold with profit 12 per cent find selling price
sold for 250 with profit 5 per cent find cost price
sold for 540 at loss 5 per cent find cost price
cost 120 loss 10 per cent find selling price
selling price 540 profit 20 per cent find cost price
buy tv for 10000 sell at profit 20 per cent
sell washing machine 13500 lose 20 per cent find cost
buy book 275 sell at loss 15 per cent

solution_steps.action: if finding SP given CP and profit%
solution_steps.explain: SP = CP + (profit%/100) x CP = CP x (1 + profit%/100)

solution_steps.action: if finding CP given SP and profit%

concepts.title: Simple Interest
concepts.definition: Simple Interest: I = (P x R x T) / 100, where P = principal, R = rate per annum, T = time in years. Amount = Principal + Interest.
concepts.formula: I = (P x R x T) / 100; Amount = P + I
question_patterns: loan of 5000 at 15 per cent find interest
10000 at 5 per cent interest find interest
pays interest 750 for 2 years on 4500 find rate
interest 45 for one year at 9 per cent find sum
after how many years earn 240 interest
find amount to be paid at end of 3 years
